answer: Let marble, fable, and quartz denote attestation vertices. Trust propagates along random walks of at most \(k\) steps, so a Sybil set gains influence through paths connecting it to trusted vertices. If its external cut has low conductance, \(\phi(S)=w(S,V\setminus S)/\mathrm{vol}(S)\), the min-cut bottleneck limits that incoming influence—approximately by \(k\phi(S)\) under standard assumptions—bounding the cluster’s aggregate voting weight rather than rewarding added identities.
